`huer` is an `httr2`-based R client for the **Philips Hue CLIP API v2** and
**Hue Bridge Pro** local HTTPS endpoints. It wraps all `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`,
and `DELETE` resource operations across 41 CLIP v2 and Bridge Pro resource
types, parses JSON envelopes into tidy `tbl_json` tables via `tidyjson`, and
provides clear diagnostics powered by `cli`.

## Discovering and Authenticating with a Bridge

1. Locate your bridge's local IP address using `hue_discover()` (or check your
   router / Hue app).
2. Press the physical round link button on top of the Hue Bridge.
3. Generate an application key (`hue-application-key`) within 30 seconds:

```{r auth, eval = FALSE}
library(huer)

bridges <- hue_discover()
ip <- bridges$internalipaddress[[1]]

# Press the physical link button on the Hue Bridge before running:
creds <- hue_create_app_key(ip, app_name = "huer")

# Store credentials for the current R session
hue_auth(ip = ip, app_key = creds$username[[1]], verify_ssl = FALSE)
```

For reproducible scripts, set `HUE_BRIDGE_IP` and `HUE_APP_KEY` in your
environment, or create an explicit client object with `hue_bridge()`:

```{r client}
library(huer)

bridge <- hue_bridge(
  ip = "192.168.1.50",
  app_key = "example-application-key",
  verify_ssl = FALSE
)
bridge
```

> **TLS Note:** Local Philips Hue Bridges serve HTTPS using a certificate
> signed by the Signify Hue Bridge Root CA. For strict certificate validation,
> pass the path to the Signify Root CA PEM file via `ca_cert` with
> `verify_ssl = TRUE`; on trusted local LANs, `verify_ssl = FALSE` disables
> certificate verification.

## Exploring All CLIP API v2 & Bridge Pro Endpoints

Use `hue_endpoints()` to inspect the complete matrix of supported resource
types, REST paths, HTTP methods, and Bridge Pro / Hue Secure additions:

```{r endpoints}
ep <- hue_endpoints()
nrow(ep)
head(ep, 10)
```

Filter for endpoints introduced for **Hue Bridge Pro** (such as MotionAware
virtual motion areas, `service_group`, `wifi_connectivity`, `speaker`, and
Hue Secure sensors):

```{r bridge-pro}
ep[ep$bridge_pro, c("resource", "category", "get", "post", "put", "delete")]
```

## Controlling Lights and Building Payloads

`hue_payload_light()` constructs validated CLIP API v2 update payloads for
`hue_update_light()` and `hue_update_grouped_light()`:

```{r payload}
payload <- hue_payload_light(
  on = TRUE,
  brightness = 75,
  mirek = 320,
  dynamics_duration = 500
)
str(payload)
```

```{r light-control, eval = FALSE}
lights <- hue_get_lights()
hue_update_light(lights$id[[1]], body = payload)

# Recall a scene with a 1-second transition
scenes <- hue_get_scenes()
hue_recall_scene(scenes$id[[1]], action = "active", duration = 1000)
```

## Working with `tidyjson` Responses

Every API response from `huer` is parsed through `hue_parse_response()` into a
`tbl_json` object (which inherits from `tibble`). Scalar and nested object
properties are spread into columns automatically, while nested arrays (such as
`children`, `services`, or `actions`) remain accessible through
`hue_unnest_array()`:

```{r tidyjson-demo}
sample_room <- paste0(
  '{"errors":[],"data":[{"id":"room-01","type":"room",',
  '"metadata":{"name":"Living Room","archetype":"living_room"},',
  '"children":[',
  '{"rid":"dev-01","rtype":"device"},',
  '{"rid":"dev-02","rtype":"device"}],',
  '"services":[{"rid":"gl-01","rtype":"grouped_light"}]}]}'
)

rooms <- hue_parse_response(sample_room)
rooms

# Expand nested arrays directly with tidyjson
hue_unnest_array(rooms, "children")
hue_unnest_array(rooms, "services")
```

Set `tidy = FALSE` on any endpoint call if you prefer the raw parsed R list.

## Hue Bridge Pro MotionAware & Real-Time EventStream

Bridge Pro turns compatible lights into MotionAware virtual motion areas. You
can manage configurations and read convenience/security motion states directly,
or subscribe to real-time updates over Server-Sent Events (`GET /eventstream/clip/v2`):

```{r motionaware, eval = FALSE}
# Bridge Pro MotionAware resources
candidates <- hue_get_motion_area_candidates()
configs <- hue_get_motion_area_configurations()
convenience <- hue_get_convenience_area_motions()
security <- hue_get_security_area_motions()

# Stream live events over SSE
events <- hue_eventstream(max_events = 5L, timeout = 30)
```
